# Experiments

*Generated by `ml/train/make_experiments_doc.py` from `artifacts/experiments/*/results.json`. Reproduce with the commands in each script's docstring; all use fixed seeds. All precision values are weighted to natural class prevalence.*

**Headline.** The original design bet on a benign-only anomaly detector for novel attacks. Measured on real data, that detector does not work on CIC flow features, but the **supervised forest generalises to unseen attack families and tools**, and its **family-head uncertainty flags them as unfamiliar**. The architecture was changed to follow the evidence (ADR-1 in `docs/03_architecture.md`).

## 1. Baseline random forest (validation split)

Plain settings (100 trees, balanced class weights, 2 samples per leaf), trained on the 3.5M-flow train sample.

| operating point | precision (natural prevalence) | recall | benign FPR | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold 0.5 | 99.94% | 99.98% | 0.004% | 1.00000 |
| FPR budget 1% | 86.7% | 100.00% | 1.00% | 1.00000 |

* **In-distribution detection is saturated** (ROC-AUC 1.0000; every attack tool above 99%). It is not a result worth presenting: the time-blocked split puts early and late parts of the same attack burst on both sides.
* **Prevalence matters.** On the raw validation sample (21% attacks) precision at the 1% budget reads 96.4%; weighted to the real class balance (7.7% attacks) it is **86.7%**. All reported precision is weighted.
* The 1% false-alarm budget in the original plan is far too loose for a SOC: at this network's size it is thousands of false alarms per hour. See the operating curve below.

## 2. Class imbalance

Binary head, 1M-row train subsample (validation, threshold 0.5):

| weights | precision | recall | benign FPR |
|---|---|---|---|
| no_weights | 99.991% | 99.955% | 0.0024% |
| balanced_subsample | 99.981% | 99.977% | 0.0051% |

Family head (attack flows only; training counts Botnet 98,922, BruteForce 64,899, DDoS 499,657, DoS 320,293, Infiltration 35,131, WebAttack 194):

| strategy | train rows | macro-F1 | recall Botnet | recall BruteForce | recall DDoS | recall DoS | recall Infiltration | recall WebAttack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no_weights | 1,019,096 | 1.0000 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% |
| balanced_subsample | 1,019,096 | 1.0000 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% |
| smote_to_5000 | 1,023,902 | 1.0000 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% |

**Finding:** every strategy, including SMOTE for the rare families, scores macro-F1 = 1.0000 on validation: the data is separable enough that imbalance handling cannot be measured in-distribution. **Decision:** keep plain class weights (cheap, no synthetic data, no leakage risk) and spend the effort on the held-out experiments below.

## 3. Shortcut features

The top features of the baseline are TCP initial window sizes: a Kali-attacker vs Windows-victim fingerprint, not attack behaviour. Validation recall at a 0.1% FPR (1M-row models):

| feature set | features | recall @ 0.1% FPR | weakest tool (>=100 flows) | its recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all_46 | 46 | 99.993% | Infiltration - NMAP Portscan | 99.2% |
| plus_dst_port | 47 | 100.000% | Botnet Ares | 100.0% |
| minus_init_window | 44 | 99.993% | Infiltration - NMAP Portscan | 99.2% |
| minus_tcp_flags | 37 | 99.993% | Infiltration - NMAP Portscan | 99.2% |
| minus_window_and_flags | 35 | 99.992% | Infiltration - NMAP Portscan | 99.1% |

**Finding:** removing the window sizes, the TCP flags, or both changes nothing in-distribution, and adding `dst_port` does not help, so it stays excluded. In-distribution tests cannot reveal a shortcut, so the same ablation was repeated under leave-one-family-out (recall at a 0.5% FPR):

| feature set | features | DoS | DDoS | BruteForce | Infiltration | Botnet |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all_46 | 46 | 97.4% | 100.0% | 99.8% | 9.7% | 100.0% |
| minus_init_window | 44 | 98.9% | 100.0% | 95.0% | 18.1% | 99.9% |
| minus_window_and_flags | 35 | 97.1% | 100.0% | 0.3% | 14.1% | 97.9% |
| behavioural_core | 31 | 99.0% | 100.0% | 1.0% | 12.4% | 97.4% |

**Finding:** without the OS-fingerprint features the model still catches unseen DoS, DDoS and Botnet, so it recognises attack *behaviour*. **SSH brute force depends on the TCP-flag counts** (connection set-up and teardown patterns, which are legitimate behaviour, not a host fingerprint).

## 4. Benign-only IsolationForest (the original novelty idea)

Trained on 500k benign train flows; scored on validation; threshold = 99.5th benign percentile (0.5% false alarms):

| config | settings | ROC-AUC (attack vs benign) | attack recall @ 0.5% FPR |
|---|---|---|---|
| n100_s256 | {'n_estimators': 100, 'max_samples': 256} | 0.720 | 0.02% |
| n300_s256 | {'n_estimators': 300, 'max_samples': 256} | 0.703 | 0.00% |
| n200_s2048 | {'n_estimators': 200, 'max_samples': 2048} | 0.856 | 0.05% |
| n200_s8192 | {'n_estimators': 200, 'max_samples': 8192} | 0.868 | 0.27% |
| n200_s2048_f05 | {'n_estimators': 200, 'max_samples': 2048, 'max_features': 0.5} | 0.855 | 0.06% |
| n200_s256_f03 | {'n_estimators': 200, 'max_samples': 256, 'max_features': 0.3} | 0.714 | 0.01% |

**Finding: it does not work on these flow features.** ROC-AUC 0.70-0.87 and essentially no attack is flagged at a usable false-alarm rate. Flood and brute-force flows look like ordinary individual flows; what makes them attacks is volume, which a per-flow detector cannot see. **Decision:** the IsolationForest is optional in the bundle format and is *not* part of the CIC decision rule. It is kept for the binary LUFlow bundle, where the `outlier` label gives it a fair test (section 8).

## 5. Generalisation to attacks the model has never seen (validation split, single seed)

Both heads are retrained WITHOUT the held-out unit; thresholds come from validation benign flows. `labelled novel` = share of the detected held-out flows the family head was unsure about. `seen ceiling` = the same model trained WITH the unit.

**Leave-one-family-out** (a whole family removed):

| held out | flows | recall @ 0.01% FPR | recall @ 0.05% FPR | recall @ 0.1% FPR | recall @ 0.5% FPR | labelled novel (0.1%) | seen ceiling (0.1%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DoS | 201,584 | 32.1% | 77.3% | 90.5% | 97.8% | 100% | 100.0% |
| DDoS | 162,035 | 70.1% | 84.1% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100% | 100.0% |
| BruteForce | 12,061 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% | 11.0% | 0% | 100.0% |
| Infiltration | 3,074 | 4.2% | 6.1% | 6.4% | 11.9% | 100% | 99.1% |
| Botnet | 19,299 | 0.0% | 97.0% | 99.9% | 100.0% | 100% | 100.0% |

**Tool holdout** (one tool removed, sibling tools remain):

| held out | flows | recall @ 0.01% FPR | recall @ 0.05% FPR | recall @ 0.1% FPR | recall @ 0.5% FPR | labelled novel (0.1%) | seen ceiling (0.1%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DDoS-HOIC | 127,674 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100% | 100.0% |
| DDoS-LOIC-HTTP | 34,188 | 0.0% | 90.1% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100% | 100.0% |
| DoS Hulk | 199,127 | 54.5% | 99.5% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100% | 100.0% |
| DoS GoldenEye | 1,507 | 0.2% | 10.4% | 75.5% | 99.9% | 100% | 100.0% |
| DoS Slowloris | 950 | 0.1% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 100% | 100.0% |

* Familiar attacks are mislabelled "novel" only 0.3%-1.9% of the time at the 0.1% budget (by construction ~2%).
* **The supervised forest generalises** to unseen floods, DoS and botnet traffic at strict false-alarm budgets, and the family head's low confidence marks those detections as unfamiliar. This is the evidence for "catches what signatures miss".
* **It does not generalise to low-and-slow families**: SSH brute force and internal Nmap scanning (Infiltration) are mostly missed when held out. Say so in the pitch.
* Recall at the strictest budgets swings between seeds (the min-max ranges); report ranges, never a single run.

## 6. Hyper-parameter search

In-distribution validation is saturated, so configs were scored by **tool-holdout recall** at a strict budget (mean over DDoS-LOIC-HTTP, DoS Hulk, DoS GoldenEye, DoS Slowloris; DDoS-HOIC is excluded so the headline demo tool is an untouched check). 14 random configs, 600k-row training subsample, validation only:

| rank | config | mean recall @0.05% FPR | @0.01% FPR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | {'max_depth': None, 'min_samples_leaf': 20, 'max_features': 0.5, 'class_weight': None} | 0.749 | 0.263 |
| 2 | {'max_depth': 16, 'min_samples_leaf': 100, 'max_features': 0.5, 'class_weight': None} | 0.737 | 0.159 |
| 3 | {'max_depth': 16, 'min_samples_leaf': 100, 'max_features': 0.2, 'class_weight': None} | 0.673 | 0.155 |
| 4 | {'max_depth': 16, 'min_samples_leaf': 20, 'max_features': 0.5, 'class_weight': None} | 0.661 | 0.263 |
| 5 | {'max_depth': 24, 'min_samples_leaf': 20, 'max_features': 0.5, 'class_weight': 'balanced_subsample'} | 0.647 | 0.263 |
| 6 | {'max_depth': 10, 'min_samples_leaf': 100, 'max_features': 0.2, 'class_weight': 'balanced_subsample'} | 0.629 | 0.171 |

Confirmation over 3 fresh seeds (the single-run ranking is noisy):

| candidate | config | mean recall @0.05% | range over seeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | {'max_depth': None, 'min_samples_leaf': 2, 'max_features': 'sqrt', 'class_weight': 'balanced_subsample'} | 0.485 | 0.46-0.53 |
| top1 | {'max_depth': None, 'min_samples_leaf': 20, 'max_features': 0.5, 'class_weight': None} | 0.631 | 0.51-0.71 |
| top2 | {'max_depth': 16, 'min_samples_leaf': 100, 'max_features': 0.5, 'class_weight': None} | 0.610 | 0.49-0.74 |
| top3 | {'max_depth': 16, 'min_samples_leaf': 100, 'max_features': 0.2, 'class_weight': None} | 0.650 | 0.53-0.75 |

**Decision:** the three tuned configs are statistically indistinguishable (all about +0.15 over the default). The smallest and fastest (depth 16, 100-sample leaves, 20% of features per split) was frozen. DDoS-LOIC-HTTP stays near 0% at the strictest budget in every configuration: tuning cannot fix that.
